summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run: the simulation status is skipped, with simulation_allowed=false, input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false and comparison_valid=false. The selected scenario is the Section 3 IGBT module simulation (two 11.2 mm x 11.2 mm x 0.3 mm silicon dies on a die attach, Cu/AlN/Cu stack, solder and Al base plate, on a cold plate through a 50 um TIM). The paper modelled it as a 3D transient FloTHERM study of two-point RthJC versus TDIM structure-function RthJC. The proposed experiment kind was custom_2d_steady, which has no transient trace, and its floorplan and power_w were empty, so the input validator rejected it (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object). The scenario also fails on physical grounds. It is a layered 3D vertical stack, and its observables (Zth curves, structure functions, TDIM divergence, probe points Ch0-Ch4) are transient and have no steady 2D counterpart. The power is ambiguous (100 W in the text versus 50 W in the Figure 4 caption), and no x/y block placement is published. No Studio result exists, so no numerical comparison with the paper is made and none is valid. The paper's reported values (RthJA 0.52, 0.36 and 0.28 K/W for TIM 0.2, 1 and 4 W/mK at Ch0; two-point RthJC 0.13 and 0.45 K/W; TDIM RthJC about 0.17-0.18 K/W) remain unreproduced and unchecked here. At most, qualitative sensitivity can be noted: the paper reports that lower TIM conductivity raises junction-to-ambient resistance and that the RthJC metric depends strongly on probe position. That is a statement about the paper, not a Studio finding. The evidence also lacks pinned page or asset locators and adversarial/independent review is unresolved. The final verdict is therefore no valid reproduction and no claim of replication.
limitations: Studio did not run, so there is no simulated output of any kind to compare with the paper.
comparison_valid is false, so no numerical comparison against the paper's RthJA, two-point RthJC or TDIM RthJC values is permitted.
The custom 2D steady experiment had an empty floorplan and no power_w, and a steady run would in any case produce no transient trace, Zth curve or structure function.

Mismatch: the paper simulates a layered 3D stack with vertical heat spreading, whereas Studio is a 2D chip floorplan solver; no x/y block positions are published for the dies, copper, ceramic or base plate.

Mismatch: the paper's observables are transient and structure-function based (Zth, Cauer/Foster networks, TDIM divergence threshold), and the Ch0-Ch4 virtual probe points have no counterpart in a 2D package model.

Mismatch: the cooling boundary is a cold plate with a constant HTC of 3000 W/m2K and a 50 um TIM of varied conductivity (0.2, 1, 4 W/mK), and the Studio package and material assumptions are not stated.
The power is inconsistent in the paper (100 W in the text versus 50 W in the Figure 4 caption), so no power row could be assigned reliably.
No usable linked asset exists: the cited links are commercial product pages, a datasheet and standards, not the FloTHERM model, mesh, ambient or solver settings, and none are pinned or available.
Evidence entries lack valid page or asset locators, no cited steady/transient regime is recorded, and the adversarial code/parameters/config/data checks and independent review are unresolved.
Digitized figure values (Figures 5-10) are not recorded with provenance and uncertainty; paper numbers come from text and annotations only, and the TDIM threshold gives 0.17 to 0.19 K/W.
This is not a replication and the result must not be read as confirming or refuting the paper's findings.
